senses.gloss: m.(b. h.; a contr. of דברברן , v. דְּבַר) [leader,] goad, the iron point on the staff (מַלְמֵד); also the spud at the end of the handle of the ploughshare (v. Sm. Ant. s. vv. Aratrum a Catrinos).
units: <cite ref="Chagigah 3b:2">Ḥag. 3ᵇ</cite> <he>מה ד׳ זה וכ׳</he> as the goad directs the cow &c.
<cite ref="Mishnah Kelim 9:6">Kel. IX, 6</cite> <he>מלמד שבלע הד׳</he> a goad (handle) in which the iron point was driven in so that nothing could be seen of it.

<cite ref="Tosefta Keilim Metsia 4:4">Tosef. Kel. B. Mets. IV, 4</cite>. Pesik. Baḥod. p. 153ᵃ; <cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Sanhedrin 10:1:21">Y. Snh. X, 28ᵃ</cite>, a. e., v. <cite ref="D00341"><he>דּוּר</he> I</cite>.

<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Sanhedrin 10:1:21">Ib.</cite> <he>אדם עושה ד׳ לפרתו וכ׳</he> man makes a goad to direct his cow, and to his (evil) inclination should he not &c.?—Pl. <he>דָּרְבֹנוֹת</he>, <he>דָּרְבוֹנוֹת</he>.

<cite ref="Kohelet Rabbah 12:11:1">Koh. R. to XII, 11</cite>; <cite ref="Bamidbar Rabbah 15">Num. R. s. 15</cite> (quoted fr. Koh. l. c.); a. fr. [<cite ref="Bamidbar Rabbah 14:4">Num. R. s. 14</cite> <he>א״ת כד׳ אלא כדרבנות</he>, v. <cite ref="K00098"><he>כַּד</he> I</cite>.]
